# loki: Copilot instructions

## Project overview

loki (Local Offline Knowledge Index) is a Python CLI tool that manages a self-hosted, fully offline AI stack. It combines llama.cpp's `llama-server` (local LLM inference), Open WebUI (chat interface), and Kiwix (offline Wikipedia and other ZIM archives), orchestrated via Docker Compose. Every service runs in a container; `llama-server` is built locally against ROCm for one AMD GPU architecture from a pinned llama.cpp commit. Optional Strata engines each serve one mixture-of-experts model, optional stable-diffusion.cpp engines each serve one image model, and a gateway publishes every engine as one API while letting only one hold the GPU. A single `loki setup` command installs all prerequisites and configures the stack from `config.yaml`.

## Architecture

- `loki/cli.py`: Click CLI entry point (`setup`, `start`, `stop`, `status`, `kill`, `update`, `cleanup`)
- `loki/config.py`: Pydantic config models, path helpers, and file generators for `Caddyfile`, `.env`, and `compose.engines.yaml`
- `loki/presets.py`: Assembles per-model `preset.ini` files under `llama.models_dir` into the `models.ini` router preset, resolving and checking file paths
- `loki/system.py`: Subprocess-backed system operations: package installation, Docker install, AMD GPU device check, shell profile editing, mDNS announcement via `avahi-publish-address`
- `llama/Dockerfile`: Two-stage build of `llama-server` with the HIP backend; the runtime stage carries only the ROCm libraries the binary links against and the BLAS kernels for the target GPU
- `gateway/gateway.py`: aiohttp service that merges the text engines' `/v1/models` (an engine that lists nothing or is unreachable keeps its last listing), routes inference by model id (from the JSON body, or the form fields of a multipart image edit) (rejecting a path the model's engine does not serve), unloads the other engines before a swap (an engine's type is its name up to the first hyphen), loads the `preload` text model (`LOKI_PRELOAD`) in the background at startup, and serves the live Strata engine's web dashboard read-only at `/strata/` (Caddy routes `http://loki.local/strata` there); built into `loki-gateway:<hash of its sources>`
- `strata/Dockerfile` and `strata/entrypoint.py`: Strata built from a pinned commit with AMD's TheRock ROCm wheels; the entrypoint merges the engine config named under `strata.engines` with the image's engine paths and starts the server unloaded
- `config.yaml`: User-edited source of truth for URL, ports, engine build settings, llama-server default options, the preload model, the Kokoro text-to-speech server, and ZIM files
- `compose.yaml`: Docker Compose stack definition (gateway, llama-server, Open WebUI, Kiwix, Caddy)
- `image/Dockerfile`: stable-diffusion.cpp's `sd-server` built against ROCm from a pinned commit for one GPU architecture
- `image/sd_supervisor.py`: Runs `sd-server` on a private port only while it has work, since an idle `sd-server` keeps GPU memory after its first generation; offers Strata's `/health` and `/unload` so the gateway unloads both alike
- `compose.engines.yaml`: Generated overlay with one `strata-<name>` service per `strata.engines` entry and one `image-<name>` service per `image.engines` entry (each kind shares one image), plus a CPU-only `kokoro` service when `tts.enabled` is set
- `tools/kiwix_tool.py`: Open WebUI tool definition (Python class) for querying the Kiwix server; paste into Workspace → Tools to expose offline archives to the LLM. Its `Tools` methods use reST `:param:` docstrings because Open WebUI builds parameter descriptions from those lines
- `tools/image_studio.py`: Open WebUI pipe function offering Image Studio Draft, Production, and Refine models, each also in a Turbo version on Qwen Image 2.1 Turbo, that send prompts and images straight to the gateway's image API; Open WebUI modules are imported at runtime because they exist only in its container
- `data/kiwix/`: ZIM files downloaded by `loki setup`
- `Caddyfile`, `.env`, `models.ini`, and `compose.engines.yaml`: Generated by `loki setup` and `loki start`; never edited by hand

## Code conventions

- Python 3.11+; use modern type hints (`list[str]`, `Path | None`)
- Pydantic v2 for config validation (`model_validate`); config models forbid unknown keys
- CLI output goes to stdout via `click.echo`; errors use `click.echo(..., err=True)`
- `subprocess.run(..., check=False)` for external commands; handle non-zero returns explicitly
- Invalid input raises or fails with a clear message instead of falling back to a different value
- Local image tags name every build input (GPU target, ROCm version, commit, or gateway source hash); commands build only images whose tag is missing and never rebuild one in place
- No logging framework; keep output minimal and user-facing

## Build and test

```bash
pip install -e ".[dev]"
pytest
```

Tests live in `tests/` and use `pytest-mock`; gateway tests use `pytest-aiohttp` against fake engines. `pyproject.toml` puts `gateway/`, `strata/`, `image/`, and `tools/` on the pytest path because the container entry scripts and the Open WebUI tool are standalone modules outside the `loki` package. The `sample_config` fixture in `conftest.py` provides a standard `LokiConfig`, and autouse fixtures redirect generated-file paths to a temporary directory and stub `subprocess.run`. Another autouse fixture reports every local image as present; image tests set its `return_value`. Mock `subprocess.run`, `requests.get`, and file I/O rather than hitting real services.

## Code quality

**Formatter and linter:** `ruff` (configured in `pyproject.toml`).

```bash
ruff format .          # format in place
ruff check --fix .     # lint with auto-fix
```

Enabled rule sets: `E/W` (pycodestyle), `F` (pyflakes), `I` (isort), `N` (naming), `UP` (pyupgrade), `B` (bugbear), `S` (bandit), `D` (pydocstyle). Docstring convention is **numpy**. `S603`/`S607` are globally ignored because all subprocess calls use hardcoded system commands. The one intentional `shell=True` vendor-install call carries an inline `# noqa: S602`.

**Type checker:** `pyright` in standard mode over `loki`, `tools`, `gateway`, `strata`, and `image` (configured in `pyproject.toml`).

```bash
pyright
```

**Pre-commit:** `.pre-commit-config.yaml` runs `ruff-format`, `ruff`, and `pyright` on every commit. Install hooks once with:

```bash
pre-commit install
```
